body: @annevk Here's the PR for the new custom element registry attribute.
This should probably have [serialization steps](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#serialising-html-fragments) similar to `shouldAppendRegistryAttribute` for `shadowrootcustomelementregistry` as well.

> I thought about the serialization steps, but when I read through these lines in serializing an element, I thought all attributes are serialized automatically. Am I missing something here?

Sure, but calling `.createElement('x-foo', { customElementRegistry: nonGlobalRegistry })` doesn't actually set that attribute (besides it could just be removed after as well).

This actually pretty similar to the `is` attribute in element serialization steps too, in that an element's "is" value is not actually reflected as an attribute. Also like the `is` attribute we might opt not to emit it if there is already a `customelementregistry` attribute.

> In this case, initialize will give foo and bar scoped registry.

That depends how `foo` and `bar` were created, if they were parsed from the main document then their custom element registry would be the global one anyway so `.initialize` would be an effective no-op on them.

However if they didn't have a registry then yes I'd expect the change in registry would result in a change in serialization (just like any other DOM change).

I believe the intended behavior of cusomelementregistry attribute is that the element with such attribute and the subtree of the element should all get null registry. The foo and bar in above example should get scoped registry, and it sounds like we do want the attribute serialized for foo and bar.

What if we don’t do the initialize and left foo and bar’s registry null? Should they get the attribute during serialization as well in this case?

> I believe the intended behavior of cusomelementregistry attribute is that the element with such attribute and the subtree of the element should all get null registry. Actually that makes sense, it seems fine to avoid serializing the attribute if the registry is the same as the parent element. > What if we don’t do the initialize and left foo and bar’s registry null? Should they get the attribute during serialization as well in this case? So I think the serialization is somewhat non-trivial, and we should also carefully consider the possibility of some kind of "declarative custom element registry" in future, with that in mind I think we should go along some lines of:
↓parent \ child→ global registry custom registry 1 custom registry 2 null
global registry no attribute attribute attribute
custom registry 1 ??? no attribute !!!attribute !!!attribute
null ??? !!!attribute !!!no attribute
Ideally we should have some story for global registry as a child of a scoped registry (??? in the table), as both it's not clear how to serialize it, and people transitioning to scoped registries will likely come across places where they need to opt-out. As a bikeshed perhaps just: ```html
``` Now in the chart I've put !!! in front of entries that, while all could be omitted, may have impacts on a possible future declarative custom element registries. e.g. If in future we have something like: ```html ....
``` then those entries with !!! may need special consideration for how it would interact with such a possible feature.

If we don't want to over complex the serialization cases, should we consider keeping it to just whichever element has the attribute will get the attribute at serialization. Without considering tree mutation, the elements registry will only be global registry or null due to shadow root attribute/element attribute, and this could be reflected in serialization by serializing the attribute when it presents.

I see the appeal, but I think I'd like to strike a balance where we make some effort to set it when we encounter a node that needs it (and doesn't already have it) and then ignore it for the remainder of that node's subtree.

Apologies for dropping the ball on this one. I’ve addressed the comments, and regarding the serialization, I think a balanced approach would be to serialize the attribute at the boundary of a registry change, as outlined in the PR. Would love to get feedback and get things rolling again :)

This was previously (and is implemented as in Safari 27/Chrome ~150) `customelementregistry`. That matches the element property. Calling is `scopedcustomelementregistry` here seems unfortunate.
@sorvell That seems like a bug. Could you help add WPT coverage on this particular behavior?
@annevk Friendly ping on this issue :)
Is it worth deprecating `shadowrootcustomelementregistry` and making `scopedcustomelementregistry` have special behaviour on `<template shadowrootmode="…">`?

I know bikeshedding is dull, but I think `initialcustomelementregistry` is a better name.

- Still leaves it open for future values.
- Makes it clear that this only sets the initial value.

I think this makes it clearer that:

```js
document.body.setAttribute('initialcustomelementregistry', '');
```

…isn't expected to work. You're too late to set the 'initial' value - it already has one. Whereas that clue isn't there with `scopedcustomelementregistry`.

Edit: Oh haha I see this has been discussed already https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12000#discussion_r3549814792. Well, I still think `initialcustomelementregistry` is better.

I rebased onto main and pushed some commits on top:

- 14726bf is the PR rebased as one commit. Main now reads `is` from the sanitized attributes, and `keepRegistryNull` does the same, so an attribute the sanitizer drops has no effect.
- acb88fb renames the attribute back to `customelementregistry`, the name Safari and Chrome ship, and reflects it as `htmlCustomElementRegistry`, as `customElementRegistry` already returns the element's registry. Since reflection is not super important here this seems like the best compromise.
- b025e69 has editorial fixes.
- 799d406 makes `initialize()` clear keep custom element registry null when it gives an element a registry, so an element can't have both.
- 29a7512 makes the `outerHTML` getter treat an exclusive `DocumentFragment` parent like no parent, so such an element serializes its registry boundary like a detached one.

There's also one thing where I wasn't sure what we should be doing:

- The XML parser honors the attribute, but only HTML serialization writes it, so in XML documents `innerHTML` loses registry boundaries. Should we extend XML serialization in DOM Parsing?

Thoughts on any of this?
I also added test coverage for the case @sorvell brought up.
